source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Digestion and Absorption
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: The proteolytic enzyme trypsin is released from the pancreas and becomes active in the
questions.explanation: Trypsinogen is activated in the duodenum; trypsin then digests proteins in the small intestine.

questions.stem: Enterokinase of the intestinal mucosa converts trypsinogen into
questions.explanation: Enterokinase (enteropeptidase) clips trypsinogen to trypsin, which then activates other pancreatic zymogens.

questions.stem: Reconstituted triglycerides leave the villus mainly as chylomicrons into the
questions.explanation: Long-chain fats are packaged as chylomicrons and enter the lacteal, not the villus blood capillary.

questions.stem: The dental formula of a permanent human dentition is written as
questions.explanation: Each half-jaw has 2 incisors, 1 canine, 2 premolars and 3 molars (32 teeth in all).

questions.stem: Brunner's glands that pour an alkaline mucus into the gut lie in the submucosa of the
questions.explanation: Duodenal (Brunner's) glands protect the mucosa from acidic chyme entering from the stomach.

questions.stem: Bile salts aid fat digestion chiefly by
questions.explanation: Bile has no digestive enzyme; bile salts emulsify fats so lipase can act on a larger surface.

questions.stem: Emulsified dietary fats are hydrolysed mainly by
questions.explanation: Pancreatic lipase is the principal enzyme that splits triglycerides in the small intestine.

questions.stem: Secretin released from the duodenal mucosa mainly stimulates the pancreas to secrete
questions.explanation: Secretin raises pancreatic HCO3- output so acidic chyme is neutralised; CCK drives enzyme release.

questions.stem: Among the three major foodstuffs, the highest bomb-calorimeter value (kcal/g) belongs to
questions.explanation: Fats yield about 9.45 kcal/g in a bomb calorimeter, far more than carbohydrates or proteins.

questions.stem: Yellowing of skin and sclera in jaundice is caused by deposition of
questions.explanation: Bilirubin and related bile pigments accumulate in blood and tissues when bile flow or liver function fails.

questions.stem: Maltase, sucrase and lactase that complete sugar digestion are secreted in the
questions.explanation: These disaccharidases occur in succus entericus on the small-intestinal brush border.

questions.stem: Hydrochloric acid of gastric juice is secreted by the
questions.explanation: Oxyntic cells secrete HCl and Castle's intrinsic factor; chief cells secrete pepsinogen.

questions.stem: Glucose and amino acids leave the villus through blood capillaries, whereas most long-chain fats leave through lacteals. The blood from the gut then reaches the liver first via the
questions.explanation: Absorbed monosaccharides and amino acids travel in the hepatic portal vein; chylomicrons travel in lymph to the thoracic duct.

questions.stem: Which enzyme is absent from pancreatic juice but present in intestinal juice?
questions.explanation: Pancreas secretes amylase, lipase and nucleases; sucrase is a brush-border intestinal enzyme.

questions.stem: Which of the following is secreted as an inactive zymogen?
questions.explanation: Pepsinogen is the inactive precursor; HCl converts it to pepsin so the stomach does not digest itself.

questions.stem: Fructose is absorbed from the small intestine mainly by
questions.explanation: Fructose uses facilitated carriers; glucose and galactose use secondary active transport with sodium.

questions.stem: A digestive enzyme is not secreted by the wall of the
questions.explanation: The oesophagus only conducts the bolus by peristalsis; it does not produce digestive enzymes.

questions.stem: The pancreas is described as a mixed gland because it secretes
options: both an exocrine juice and endocrine hormones
questions.explanation: Acini pour digestive juice into the duodenum; islets release insulin and glucagon into blood.

questions.stem: Which statement about human bile is correct?
options: It contains lipase as its main enzyme
It is stored and concentrated in the gall bladder
It is produced by the pancreas
It activates pepsinogen in the stomach
questions.explanation: Hepatocytes make bile; the gall bladder stores it. Bile salts emulsify fats and do not digest protein.

questions.stem: Salivary amylase stops acting soon after the bolus reaches the stomach because
options: the enzyme is digested by lipase
gastric pH is too low for its activity
starch is already fully hydrolysed in the mouth
questions.explanation: Ptyalin works near neutrality; HCl of gastric juice inactivates it.

questions.stem: Cholecystokinin (CCK) released from the small intestine causes
options: contraction of the gall bladder and enzyme-rich pancreatic secretion
only HCl secretion by parietal cells
closure of the pyloric sphincter permanently
release of ADH from the pituitary
questions.explanation: CCK empties stored bile and stimulates pancreatic acinar enzymes when fatty chyme arrives.

questions.stem: The physiological fuel value assigned to dietary protein (kcal/g) is about
questions.explanation: Bomb value of protein is 5.65 kcal/g, but incomplete oxidation in the body gives a physiological value of 4.0.

questions.stem: Which condition is not classed as a primary disorder of the digestive tract?
questions.explanation: Emphysema is a lung disease; the others are listed digestive disorders in the chapter.

questions.stem: In infants, the gastric enzyme that curdles milk protein is
questions.explanation: Rennin coagulates casein so it stays longer in the stomach for pepsin to act.

questions.stem: Which statement about pepsin is incorrect?
options: It is formed from pepsinogen by HCl
It acts best in a strongly acidic medium
It hydrolyses proteins to proteoses and peptones
It is the main proteolytic enzyme of pancreatic juice
questions.explanation: Pepsin is gastric; pancreatic juice uses trypsin, chymotrypsin and carboxypeptidases.

questions.stem: Identify the incorrect pairing of nutrient and route of absorption from a villus.
options: Long-chain fatty acids — lacteal as chylomicrons
Vitamin B12 — lacteal without any intrinsic factor
questions.explanation: Vitamin B12 binds Castle's intrinsic factor and is absorbed in the ileum into blood, not freely into lacteals.
